title: Non-Linear Returns
equation: Focus Ratio = % of Effort on Your Top 20% Activities
hook: Most of last month's revenue probably came from a handful of things you barely spent time on.
statement: Effort rarely produces proportional results. A small slice drives most of them.
explainer: Some hours are worth ten times more than others. If most of your week goes to the low-return stuff, working harder just means more low-return hours.
sop: List everything you did last month that drove a result.
Rank them by actual output, not effort.
Work out what % of your time went to your top 20%. That's your Focus Ratio.
Move time from the bottom half to the top 20% this week.
Re-rank monthly, because your top 20% will shift.
equation_example: You spend 15% of your time on your top 20% activities. So your Focus Ratio is 15%. Higher means your effort is going where it pays off. Lower means most of your week goes to stuff that barely moves the needle.
question: Write down your top 20% for this month and block time for it first.
closing_statement: Most results come from a small slice of effort.
caption:
Principle Nº 112: Non-Linear Returns

Most of last month's revenue probably came from a handful of things you barely spent time on.

Effort rarely produces proportional results. A small slice drives most of them.

Your turn: Write down your top 20% for this month and block time for it first.
